mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite.
failure_condition: 20-day forward S&P 500 returns are not significantly higher during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: 20-day forward S&P 500 returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth coupled with high unemployment suggests a complex economic environment where equity markets may struggle, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts in a late-cycle expansion indicate strong consumer demand, which is positive for equity markets.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in late-cycle periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment rolls signal a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and equity markets.
failure_condition: 5-day forward S&P 500 returns are not significantly higher during periods of PAYEMS growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below a certain threshold indicates supply-side weakness, leading to negative equity returns.
